clue.text: Where we see worshipping convert go — any guess?

indicators.note: to convert something is to change its form, so the following letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A missionary urging someone to switch faith and take a punt on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worshipping' looks like part of the picture of conversion, but it belongs to the definition; 'convert' is the anagram signal working on GO ANY GUESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Synagogues are the buildings where Jewish congregations gather for prayer and services.

clue.text: Son and husband boarding reserved coach

indicators.note: boarding means getting on, so the husband's letter climbs aboard and sits inside the other word

parts.note: a reserved, distant manner is cool

explanation.surface: A father and son climbing onto a coach someone has booked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' looks like a bus, but here it is a verb: to train or teach.
explanation.definitionFit: To school someone is to train or instruct them, just as a coach does.

clue.text: Bit hurried

definitions.meaning: first meaning: past tense of bite, gave a small sharp pinch with the teeth
second meaning: informal British for went quickly, as in popped out to the shop

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bit' looks like a noun meaning a small piece, but it is the past tense of bite.
explanation.definitionFit: Nipped is both a past tense of pinching with the teeth and an informal British past tense for dashing somewhere quickly.

clue.text: Explosions seen this evening in sky — a gunfight we suspect

indicators.note: 'we suspect' hints the letters are not to be trusted as written and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Bangs overhead tonight that sound like a shoot-out in the sky.
explanation.walkthrough: Guy Fawkes Night, 5 November, is the British bonfire night of fireworks marking the failed 1605 plot to blow up Parliament; the clue appeared on that date.
explanation.definitionFit: The night is celebrated with firework displays, so explosions in the evening sky are its hallmark.

clue.text: Upwardly mobile British posh, attracted to wine, fall for dining here?

indicators.note: in a down clue, upwardly mobile means the letters travel up, so the whole string is read from the bottom
attracted to says one piece clings to the next, so they sit side by side

parts.note: U means upper-class, as in U and non-U
port is a fortified wine
to sag is to droop or fall

explanation.surface: A social climber, keen on wine, falling for a trendy eatery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upwardly mobile' reads as social climbing, but it reverses B, U, PORT and SAG in this down entry. A gastropub is a pub serving restaurant-quality food.
explanation.definitionFit: A gastropub is a pub known for its good food, so it is a place one might choose for a meal.

clue.text: Feel subdued, occasionally wanting escape

indicators.note: occasionally means only now and then, so only every other letter of the phrase is taken

explanation.surface: Feeling low from time to time and longing to get away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' is a link: it reads as the letters wanting, or needing, to give the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To elude someone or something is to evade or get away from it.

clue.text: Noble spy

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a titled member of the nobility, such as a lord
second meaning: to look closely or searchingly

explanation.walkthrough: One word is a noun for a titled aristocrat and a verb for looking hard.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer is a lord in the House of Lords, and to peer is to squint or look searchingly at something.

clue.text: Discharge internet task

parts.note: E stands for electronic, as in e-mail, the internet prefix
a mission is an assigned task

explanation.surface: An order to sack someone or release something, given as an online job.
explanation.definitionFit: An emission is a release or outflow of gas, light or fluid.

clue.text: Ginger wraps he had put in the microwave?

indicators.note: wraps says the first word goes around the following letters like a wrapper

parts.note: ginger hair is called red
to have a meal is to eat it, so had means ate

explanation.surface: A cat called Ginger wrapping the takeaway he had before zapping it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ginger' looks like a name or a spice; it is the colour of red hair, and 'had' means ate, as in had dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Leftovers put in a microwave are warmed up again, that is reheated; the question mark marks this as an example.

clue.text: Divine being cuddled by nymph, before mum who steps in unexpectedly

indicators.note: cuddled by puts the god right up against the fairy, close beside it
before says the god comes ahead of the mother

parts.note: a nymph is a spirit of nature, a fairy
a god is a divine being
mum is mother

explanation.surface: A goddess embraced by a nymph, ahead of a mother appearing out of nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: In pantomime and fairy tales such as Cinderella the fairy godmother appears without warning to help the heroine.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairy godmother is a benefactor who arrives out of the blue to sort out someone's troubles.

clue.text: Gleeful prince very quietly ousting bishop

indicators.note: ousting says one thing pushes the other out and takes its place

parts.note: Prince Harry
RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop
pp, pianissimo, is the musical direction for very quietly

explanation.surface: A cheerful royal hushing a churchman out of the room.
explanation.walkthrough: Bishop is usually B; here it is RR, the Right Reverend, which PP replaces.
explanation.definitionFit: Happy and gleeful are synonyms for joyful and delighted.

clue.text: Taking part in burlesque, am I shameless or strait-laced?

indicators.note: Taking part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A performer in a risque show wondering whether they are brazen or prudish.
explanation.definitionFit: Squeamish can mean easily shocked or prudish, much like someone prim and strait-laced.

clue.text: Agrarian epoch crops twice in rotation outside

indicators.note: in rotation means turning round, so the letters are read in the opposite direction
crops twice says both words are trimmed, the front of one and the end of the other, leaving a run inside

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A farming age in which fields grow crops twice under a rotation system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crops' and 'rotation' look like farming terms; they cut away AGR and CH and then turn RIANEPO round.
explanation.definitionFit: Open-air means taking place out of doors rather than inside a building.

clue.text: US area I relocated elsewhere?

indicators.note: relocated means moved to new positions, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An American region shifted somewhere else.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: from an American point of view the landmass across the oceans is elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Eurasia, the combined landmass of Europe and Asia, lies away from the USA, a cheeky example of somewhere else.

clue.text: Toy with hope for hangman's intended victim?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a child's plaything for jumping over
second meaning: a condemned person hopes the noose will skip, or miss, them

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase as a rope that skips its job, the escape a person facing the noose would wish for.
explanation.definitionFit: A skipping rope is a playground toy, and read as a rope that skips you it is the gallows victim's wish.

clue.text: Smart German car tooted, abruptly muffled

parts.note: in means fashionable or smart
Audi is a German car make

indicators.note: abruptly means cut short, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: to toot a horn is to blow it, so tooted is blew

explanation.surface: A posh German car sounding its horn with a sudden, deadened note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abruptly' shortens BLEW to BLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A muffled sound is deadened and so may be impossible to hear clearly.

clue.text: Jeering now and then, loud fans riot — case overturned

indicators.note: overturned means turned upside down, which in a down entry reads the letters from the bottom
now and then means only at intervals, so only every other letter is kept

explanation.surface: Mocking crowds sometimes, as noisy supporters riot after a court ruling is reversed.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking every other letter of LOUD FANS RIOT CASE gives LUFNROCS, which 'overturned' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone scornful mocks and derides, which is what a jeering crowd does.

clue.text: Outlaw concealing ecstasy packets in soft seating

indicators.note: concealing means hiding, so the drug's letter is tucked inside

parts.note: to outlaw is to ban
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
bags are packets or small sacks

explanation.surface: Banning a drug hidden in bags stuffed in comfy chairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Beanbags are large floppy cushions filled with beads, used as informal chairs.

clue.text: Perhaps Derby mounts should be finishing courses

parts.note: Derby is a type of English cheese; perhaps marks it as an example
to board a vehicle or horse is to mount it

explanation.surface: Horses running in the Derby ought to be finishing their racecourses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Derby' looks like the horse race, which makes 'mounts' look like horses; Derby is in fact a cheese from Derbyshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheeseboards are served at the end of a meal, so they are the closing courses of dinner.

clue.text: Really, news should cover French and Shakespearean verse

indicators.note: in a down entry, cover puts one piece on top of the next

parts.note: so means really, as in so good
N is the abbreviation for new, so news is read as N's, two Ns
et is French for and

explanation.surface: A newspaper ought to report on French and English poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'news' is read as the plural of N, the abbreviation for new, so it gives NN, which sits on top of ET in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare wrote 154 sonnets, fourteen-line poems, his best-known short verse.

clue.text: A very loud voice causes concern

parts.note: ff, fortissimo, is the musical direction for very loud
to air an opinion is to voice it, so voice gives air

explanation.surface: A booming voice prompts worry.
explanation.definitionFit: An affair is a matter or business, something that is someone's concern.

clue.text: Management in a row

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the operating or managing of a business
second meaning: consecutively, as in three days on the trot

explanation.walkthrough: 'in a row' looks like a quarrel or a line of seats; it means consecutively.
explanation.definitionFit: Running is both the noun for operating a business and an adverb for happening consecutively.

clue.text: Vulgar ad's single characters hugged by guy

indicators.note: single characters says the two letters of ad do not stay together: one slips further along on its own
hugged by means held in an embrace, so the letters of ad go inside the other word

parts.note: the word ad taken as written

explanation.surface: A crude advert with its letters clasped by a bloke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'single characters' means A and D go in separately: A after the G and D after the U, so it is not GADUY but the D moves on past the U.
explanation.definitionFit: Showy, garish and tasteless things are described as gaudy, close to vulgar.

clue.text: Deliver contract

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to leave goods or a passenger at a place
second meaning: to decline or shrink, as sales fall away

explanation.walkthrough: 'contract' looks like a noun for an agreement, but it is the verb for getting smaller.
explanation.definitionFit: Drop off covers both leaving goods at an address and falling away or diminishing in number.

clue.text: It may cast light on someone getting shot

definitions.text: It may cast light on someone getting shot

parts.words: It may cast light on someone getting shot
parts.note: shot means photographed, and the old single-use bulb lit the subject of the picture

explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting shot' suggests a shooting; here it is a photograph, and the device is the old disposable flash bulb.
explanation.definitionFit: Flashbulbs gave a bright burst of light so a camera could photograph a subject indoors or in the dark.

clue.text: This brings out highlights of Red Queen, beginning with 'Heads will roll!'

definitions.text: This brings out highlights of Red

indicators.note: will roll means turning over, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: Queen Anne, the British monarch

indicators.note: beginning means the start, so only the opening letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: The Red Queen of Alice in Wonderland shouting her threat of executions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads will roll!' looks like a royal threat, but 'Heads' gives H and 'will roll' turns ANNE H round.
explanation.definitionFit: Henna is a reddish dye used on hair, giving it red highlights.

clue.text: Girl in US city's heading south

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles, so the possessive gives LA'S

indicators.note: heading means the front of the word, so only its first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A young woman in Los Angeles setting off southwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading south' sounds like travelling; it is just the first letter of 'south'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lass is a mainly Scottish and northern English word for a girl or young woman.

clue.text: Device, kind used by hack?

indicators.note: used by says the first piece is put to use alongside the second, placed beside it

parts.note: a type is a kind or sort
a hack is a jobbing writer or journalist

explanation.surface: A tool of the sort a journalist relies on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hack' could be a cut or a computer intrusion; here it is a writer.
explanation.definitionFit: A typewriter is a mechanical machine for printing letters on paper, once a reporter's basic equipment.
